answer: The dining hall should stay open until 9 p.m. on weeknights instead of closing at 7. The current schedule shuts out the students who need dinner most. Evening labs and studio courses run until 7:50, so anyone in those sections misses the last hot meal three nights a week. Last spring's student government survey found that most of the students who skipped dinner named the closing time, not the food, as the reason. Some argue that a later close costs money, but the hall already keeps a dish crew until 9 to finish cleanup, so the added expense is mostly food, not labor. A two-hour extension is a small change that keeps students fed on the nights they have the least time to cook.

A four-day school week with longer days would serve students better than the current five-day schedule. Longer class periods give teachers room for the lab work and discussion that a 45-minute block cuts short. In addition, the district's pilot at two middle schools reported fewer absences, because families scheduled appointments on the free day instead of pulling students out of class. Critics point out that "a day off is a childcare problem for working parents," and that concern is fair; the district can answer it by keeping buildings open on the fifth day for supervised study and clubs. When the tradeoffs are weighed, the longer school day buys more real learning time than the fifth day it replaces.

The town should build protected bike lanes along Main Street rather than keep the painted lanes it has now. Paint does not stop a delivery truck from parking in the lane, and the traffic office logged an average of six blocked-lane complaints per week last fall. A curb or a row of planters does stop the truck, which is why the two blocks that already have barriers reported zero blockages over the same period. Business owners worry about losing parking, but the plan removes only nine spaces while adding a rack that holds thirty bikes. Protected lanes cost more than paint up front, and they are the only version that riders will actually trust.

The library should extend its hours during finals week. Many students study late and the library closes at midnight, so they have to move to the dorm lounges which are noisy. My roommate and I both had to leave the library on the last night of the semester before we finished studying. I think a 24 hour schedule for one week would not cost that much. Some people would say students should just plan better, but exams pile up in the same week no matter how you plan. Extending the hours would help students do their best on their exams.

The dining hall should start composting its food waste. Right now everything that gets scraped off a plate goes into the same bins as the plastic and paper. Composting would reduce the amount that goes to the landfill. The environmental club ran a one-day bin at lunch last year and filled three buckets with scraps from a single meal period, so the volume is definitely there. It would take some training for the staff and the students, and that is the main reason it hasn't happened yet. Overall composting is a good idea and the school should do it.

A campus shuttle to the train station would make it easier for students to get home on weekends. Students without cars now depend on rides from friends or on a taxi that costs more than the train ticket itself. A shuttle that runs on Friday afternoon and Sunday evening would cover the times when most people travel. Other colleges in the area do this already, which shows it is possible. The main objection is cost, however a shuttle could charge a small fare to help pay for the driver. This would be a helpful service for a lot of students.

There are good things about phones like looking something up quick and there are bad things like getting distracted. It really depends on the student and the teacher and the class. Everybody has an opinion on this. Its something schools have to figure out.

Parking on campus is something a lot of people talk about because there is not enough of it and the lots fill up early and then people park in the fire lane or on the grass and get tickets which makes them angry. Sophomores are not even allowed to have cars, but the lots are still full, so it is not the sophomores fault. The school keeps building new buildings on old parking lots. Something needs to change with parking. It is a problem for students and also staff and visitors too.

Whisk one cup of flour, one tablespoon of sugar, two teaspoons of baking powder, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl. In a second bowl, beat one egg with one cup of milk and two tablespoons of melted butter. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ones and stir until just combined; a few lumps are fine. Heat a skillet over medium heat and pour a quarter cup of batter for each pancake. Flip when bubbles form on the surface, cook one more minute, and serve warm with syrup or fruit.

The question of whether the campus should change its recycling program is one that comes up often, and it is worth thinking about the many different aspects of the topic from multiple perspectives. Recycling is something that many people have opinions about, and those opinions can differ quite a bit depending on who you ask and what their experiences have been. On the one hand, there are those who feel strongly that the current program is working well enough, and on the other hand, there are those who feel that it could be improved in various ways. It is also important to consider the role of the facilities staff, the students, the faculty, and the administration, since each of these groups is affected by the program in its own way and each has its own priorities. Furthermore, there are questions about cost, convenience, awareness, and participation, all of which are related to one another in complicated ways that deserve careful attention. Some campuses have tried different approaches, and the results have been mixed, which suggests that there is no single answer that fits every situation. In the end, what matters most is that the conversation continues, that all voices are heard, and that the campus keeps thinking carefully about this issue as it moves forward into the future.
